Safe diagnostic placeholders for the first milestone.
TCP check
Test whether a host and port can accept TCP connections.
Future checks can record connect latency, timeout, and route selection.
Use only for systems you own or are authorized to test.
TLS/SNI check
Verify that a TLS service presents an expected certificate.
Future checks can show SNI, certificate issuer, expiry, and handshake errors.
Use this to debug your own domains and privacy-safe connectivity issues.
HTTP check
Inspect basic HTTP availability and response status.
Future checks can show status code, redirects, timing, and selected route.
Avoid sending secrets in diagnostic URLs.
MTU test
Find packet size problems that can break VPN connections.
Future tests can estimate MTU/MSS and explain fragmentation symptoms.
Run this when websites stall or VPN traffic feels unreliable.
LAN scanner
Discover devices on your local network with safe checks.
Future discovery should be transparent, rate-limited, and limited to local networks.
Scan only networks where you have permission.
Security audit
Review defensive network posture without attack automation.
Allowed checks include Wi-Fi encryption, WPS detection, DNS audit, and exposed local services.
Treat findings as risks or misconfigurations, not proof of compromise.

Privacy and safety defaults for future features.
Local-first by default
Diagnostics, logs, and future captures should stay on this device.
This skeleton has no cloud upload paths, analytics SDKs, telemetry SDKs, ad SDKs, or tracking SDKs.
Only export logs or PCAP files after a clear user action.
Safety boundary
ViRouteFS is for defensive diagnostics and VPN routing.
Offensive features such as cracking, deauth, exploit automation, and brute force are out of scope.
Keep future tools transparent, permission-based, and rate-limited.

OpenVPN Work
Future work OpenVPN tunnel for corporate CIDR networks.
Banking apps → System
The banking app will use System inside ViRouteFS unless a separate trusted policy is configured.
If the bank requires a normal network, keep this rule above tunnel rules.
Telegram → Xray Germany
Telegram traffic will go through Xray Germany because the messenger rule matched.
Before real routing, verify the legality and stability of the selected tunnel.
YouTube → Hysteria2 NL
YouTube will go through Hysteria2 NL because the domain matched the video rule.
For video, later add DNS, TLS/SNI, HTTP, and MTU diagnostics for this route.
10.0.0.0/8 → OpenVPN Work
The address belongs to corporate network 10.0.0.0/8 and will go through OpenVPN Work.
172.16.1.0/22 → OpenVPN Work
The address belongs to corporate network 172.16.1.0/22 and will go through OpenVPN Work.
Make sure corporate CIDRs do not conflict with your home or mobile network.
Suspicious domain → Block
The domain looks like a blocked example and should not receive an outbound route.
Check the domain manually and do not open it if the source is unknown.
Default → System
Apps without rules use System route.
If another route was expected, add a more specific rule above the default rule.
